interactions.summary: Jiang turns the Piccarda scenario into a general lesson: life is too complex to map completely, so faith, intuition, and will must guide action because providence can intervene beyond human strategy.

A student asks whether faith guarantees that whatever you do will be led to the right result. Jiang rejects that simplification and says faith means trusting the intuition through which one's connection to God expresses itself, not expecting easy or automatic answers.
A student raises a new hypothetical: can love of God ever require breaking a vow to God, as when a monk sworn never to kill must stop someone about to destroy God?

claims.claim: Jiang says the Piccarda thought experiment shows that no one can fully strategize or map out life in advance, because providence can intervene in ways beyond calculation.
He says Dante's lesson is not that faith mechanically guarantees good outcomes, but that faith should orient a person toward the choice they genuinely believe is right when no easy answer exists.
Jiang defines intuition as a person's connection to God, and says that having faith in God practically means having faith in oneself and doing what one believes is right.
Jiang calls it irresponsible to flatten Dante into the slogan that faith makes everything work out, because life offers no easy answers and often requires trusting intuition over logic.
The next student hypothetical presses whether vows to God can conflict internally, by asking if a monk who vowed never to kill could justifiably kill in order to save God.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang says the thought experiment proves that you can never truly map life out, so the best guide is intuition, faith, and will rather than strategy.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you can never, ever truly strategize
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It converts Dante from a doctrinal text into a theory of action under irreducible uncertainty.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang bluntly translates faith in God into faith in yourself because intuition is your connection to God.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's sharpest reversal: divine trust becomes interior trust rather than passive dependence.

signature_moments.moment: He calls the easy slogan that faith makes everything work out irresponsible.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It shows Jiang actively policing against sentimental or deterministic readings of providence.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The inner guide Jiang prefers over explicit logic in complex moral situations; he roots it in a person's connection to God.
Not a guarantee that any action will succeed, but a way of trusting oneself to choose what feels right when life does not offer easy answers.

chronology_notes.note: On 2026-06-18 Jiang sharpens the lecture's account of providence by explicitly rejecting a simplistic 'faith makes everything work out' reading and redefining faith as intuition grounded in one's connection to God.
